{{Short description|Topological space in mathematics}}
{{no footnotes|date=September 2025}}
In [[mathematics]], in particular in [[nonlinear analysis]], a '''Fréchet manifold''' is a [[topological space]] modeled on a [[Fréchet space]] in much the same way as a [[Manifold (mathematics)|manifold]] is modeled on a [[Euclidean space]].

More precisely, a Fréchet manifold consists of a [[Hausdorff space]] <math>X</math> with an atlas of coordinate charts over Fréchet spaces whose transitions are [[Differentiation in Fréchet spaces|smooth mappings]].  Thus <math>X</math> has an [[open cover]] <math>\left\{ U_{\alpha} \right\}_{\alpha \in I},</math> and a collection of [[homeomorphism]]s <math>\phi_{\alpha} : U_{\alpha} \to F_{\alpha}</math> onto their images, where <math>F_{\alpha}</math> are [[Fréchet space]]s, such that 
<math display=block>\phi_{\alpha\beta} := \phi_\alpha \circ \phi_\beta^{-1}|_{\phi_\beta\left(U_\beta\cap U_\alpha\right)}</math> is smooth for all pairs of indices <math>\alpha, \beta.</math>

== Classification up to homeomorphism ==

It is by no means true that a finite-dimensional manifold of dimension <math>n</math> is {{em|globally}} homeomorphic to <math>\R^n</math> or even an open subset of <math>\R^n.</math>  However, in an infinite-dimensional setting, it is possible to classify "[[well-behaved]]" Fréchet manifolds up to homeomorphism quite nicely.  A 1969 theorem of David Henderson states that every infinite-dimensional, [[Separable space|separable]], [[Metric space|metric]] Fréchet manifold <math>X</math> can be [[Embedding|embedded]] as an open subset of the infinite-dimensional, separable [[Hilbert space]], <math>H</math> (up to linear isomorphism, there is only one such space).

The embedding homeomorphism can be used as a global chart for <math>X.</math>  Thus, in the infinite-dimensional, separable, metric case, up to homeomorphism, the "only" topological Fréchet manifolds are the open subsets of the separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. But in the case of {{em|differentiable}} or {{em|smooth}} Fréchet manifolds (up to the appropriate notion of diffeomorphism) this fails{{cn|date=July 2020}}.
